title: Test coverage is measured for the tool and enforced at 99%
Measure git-cicd coverage honestly, including subprocess runs
body:
Epic gcd-1ee1 (unit 7 of plan git-dev-883c, record mangimangi/git-dev .pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md). PR targets plan/git-dev-883c. First of four issues; the threshold issue and the gap-closing issue depend on this one.

## Problem
ci/test.sh runs pytest with `--cov --cov-report=term-missing --cov-config=pyproject.toml` only when pytest-cov imports; pyproject.toml has `[tool.coverage.run] include = ["git-cicd"]` and `[tool.coverage.report] show_missing = true, skip_empty = true`, no threshold. Re-measured at refinement (2026-11-28, main at v0.0.4 / de991b7, Python 3.12, coverage 7.17.5, 373 tests passing): git-cicd 63% of 1,136 statements (416 missed). That run counts only code executed in the pytest process. Tests that start the tool as a subprocess are not counted: tests/conftest.py `Repo.run` runs `[sys.executable, str(script), *args]` with cwd in a tmp repo, and `Repo.install_tool` (conftest.py ~line 76-84) first copies the script to `<tmp>/repo/.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd` so `script` is that copy; tests/test_config.py:363-364 runs SCRIPT directly; tests/test_own_jobs.py and tests/test_install.py also drive run-job/install via subprocess.

## Scope
- pyproject.toml `[tool.coverage.run]`: enable subprocess measurement (coverage >= 7.10 `patch = ["subprocess"]`, with `parallel = true` and data combined after the run) so `python3 git-cicd ...` started by a test is measured.
- Copies of the script made by `install_tool` must count as `git-cicd`: widen `include` to match the copies (e.g. `*/git-cicd`, with `source`/`include` written so the relative pattern does not depend on the subprocess cwd) and add `[tool.coverage.paths]` mapping the copied paths onto the root `git-cicd` so the report shows one row, `git-cicd`.
- ci/setup.sh: install a pytest-cov/coverage version that supports the chosen mechanism (pin a minimum, e.g. `coverage>=7.10`), into the same venv it already creates (`$CACHE/venv-$FLOOR`).
- ci/test.sh: always measure when pytest-cov is present (keep the existing fallback that runs without coverage when setup was skipped, but print a line saying coverage was not measured); combine parallel data; print the term-missing report. Keep the `exec`-free ending only if combine needs a step after pytest. Data files go to a temp/cache location, not committed; add any `.coverage*` to .gitignore if they can land in the repo.
- tests/conftest.py: only if needed for the mechanism (e.g. environment passed through `Repo.run`, which currently strips only GITHUB_/CICD_ keys and so keeps COVERAGE_* vars). No test behaviour changes.
- A local `./git-cicd check --setup` and CI give the same figure (both run ci/setup.sh + ci/test.sh on the floor 3.11).
- Docs: AGENTS.md "Running the checks" and README.md "Developing git-cicd" (the `test` row of the table at ~line 670 and the text after it) say the test job measures line coverage of git-cicd including subprocess runs and prints missing lines. README interface sections do not change.
- No threshold in this issue unless the true figure is already >= 99% (it will not be).

## Acceptance criteria
- `./git-cicd check --setup` in a clean checkout prints one coverage row for `git-cicd` with the missing lines.
- The figure counts subprocess runs: the PR description shows the figure before (63% of 1,136) and after the change, and names one function only reached through a subprocess test that is now counted.
- Running `./git-cicd check --job test` twice gives the same figure (no stale parallel data carried over).
- `./git-cicd verify` passes; generated workflows unchanged; .vendored/configs/git-cicd.json unchanged.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing; no vendor-protected file touched.
- Verdict / git-cicd:verdict passes on the PR.

## Decisions
- Mechanism: coverage's built-in `patch = ["subprocess"]` (coverage 7.10+, 7.17.5 verified to install for this suite) rather than a sitecustomize/.pth hack, because it needs no file outside pyproject.toml/ci and works on the 3.11 floor.
- Installed copies are mapped back to `git-cicd` with `[tool.coverage.paths]` rather than changing tests to stop copying, because install_tool tests the installed layout on purpose.

title: Close git-cicd coverage gaps to 99% with behaviour tests
body:
Epic gcd-1ee1 (unit 7 of plan git-dev-883c). PR targets plan/git-dev-883c. Blocked by gcd-1ee1.1 (honest measurement, subprocess runs counted); work from the figure and missing-line list that issue produces, not the in-process 63%.

## Problem
At refinement (main v0.0.4, in-process measurement) git-cicd is 63% of 1,136 statements, 416 missed; large uncovered blocks include lines 275-285, 304-314, 616-646, 675-700, 801-839, 1426-1488, 1565-1600, 1613-1689, 1708-1770, 1867-1877 (some will be covered once gcd-1ee1.1 counts subprocess runs). Re-run the report at the start of this issue and use its list.

## Scope
Add tests under tests/ (extend existing files test_config.py, test_decide.py, test_run.py, test_workflow.py, test_report.py, test_check.py, test_patterns.py, or add new test_*.py following their patterns: the `repo` fixture and `Repo` helper in tests/conftest.py, `git_cicd` module import for in-process calls, `repo.run(...)` for CLI runs) until git-cicd is at 99% line coverage or more. Tests assert behaviour a consumer relies on, not lines:
- validate: every validation error with its exact message and exit code.
- decide: every decision and its reason on each trigger (open, merge, cron, manual), including branches/paths/needs_nothing and declared inputs (defaults, choices, unknown input, bad JSON in CICD_MANUAL_INPUTS).
- run-job: pass, a failing setup, a failing step, and the results it records.
- generate and verify: each generated file (git-cicd-open.yml, -merge.yml, -cron.yml present only while a job has cron, -manual.yml), verify passing and failing on disagreement.
- report: the verdict line for every outcome.
- check: its defaults (target = upstream, else origin/HEAD, else main), --job, --setup.
- every exit code of every subcommand.
Rules:
- A gap is closed with a real test. A line is excluded (`# pragma: no cover`) only when no test can reach it, with a comment on that line saying why; the PR lists every exclusion.
- A defect a new test exposes is fixed in git-cicd together with the test that shows it and named in the PR description. Any other behaviour change to git-cicd, the README interface or the generated workflows is out of scope.
- Do not add the threshold here (gcd-1ee1.3 does).

## Acceptance criteria
- `./git-cicd check --setup` passes and its report shows git-cicd >= 99%.
- PR description lists the before/after figure, every exclusion with its reason, and every defect fixed (or says none).
- `./git-cicd verify` passes; generated workflows unchanged; README interface unchanged.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.
- Verdict / git-cicd:verdict passes on the PR.

## Decisions
- Can be split across several PRs if large, but the issue closes only when the report is >= 99%.

title: Enforce 99% coverage of git-cicd in the test job
body:
Epic gcd-1ee1 (unit 7 of plan git-dev-883c). PR targets plan/git-dev-883c. Blocked by gcd-1ee1.2 (coverage at >= 99%), which is blocked by gcd-1ee1.1.

## Scope
- pyproject.toml `[tool.coverage.report]`: add `fail_under = 99` (keep `show_missing = true`, `skip_empty = true`).
- ci/test.sh: the test step fails when coverage of git-cicd is below 99%, after printing the report with missing lines. The fallback that runs pytest without pytest-cov (setup skipped) must not silently pass the gate in CI: when `CI` is set and pytest-cov is missing, fail with a message naming `./git-cicd check --setup`; locally it may still run without coverage but prints that coverage was not checked.
- AGENTS.md ("Running the checks") and README.md ("Developing git-cicd", the `test` row at ~line 670): state the rule — the test job fails below 99% line coverage of git-cicd; a change that lowers coverage below 99% fails the verdict and adds its tests in the same pull request; a line is excluded only when no test can reach it, with a comment saying why. README interface sections do not change.

## Acceptance criteria
- `./git-cicd check --setup` in a clean checkout passes with git-cicd >= 99%.
- Removing a test file (e.g. tests/test_report.py) makes `./git-cicd check --job test` and the verdict fail with the report showing the missing lines; shown once in the PR description (output pasted), then restored.
- `./git-cicd verify` passes; generated workflows unchanged.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.
- Verdict / git-cicd:verdict passes on the PR.

## Decisions
- Threshold lives in pyproject.toml `fail_under` (single source, read by coverage), not as `--cov-fail-under` in ci/test.sh, so a local coverage run reads the same rule.

title: Add bats tests for install.sh and the ci/ scripts, run by the test job
body:
Epic gcd-1ee1 (unit 7 of plan git-dev-883c). PR targets plan/git-dev-883c. Blocked by gcd-1ee1.1 (both edit ci/setup.sh and ci/test.sh). No numeric coverage threshold for shell (decided by the owner 2026-11-28).

## Scope
Bats files under tests/bats/ (e.g. tests/bats/release.bats, update-vendored.bats, vendor-check.bats, setup.bats, test.bats, install.bats, plus a shared helper). Each test runs the real script in a temp git repo with fake vendored tools (stubs that log argv and env, like the FAKE logger in tests/test_own_jobs.py) and no network. Behaviours:
- ci/release.sh: each case of its decision — CICD_TRIGGER=manual -> `release bump` with GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=workflow_dispatch; merge whose CICD_HEAD subject starts `chore: bump version` -> `release publish`; merge with `chore: install` -> prints nothing-to-release, exit 0, release not called; any other merge -> `release bump` with GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=push; any other/unset trigger -> exit 1 with the message. And the environment it hands to `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/release`: GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE from CICD_BASE, INPUT_BUMP_TYPE / INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY / INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION from CICD_INPUT_*, GH_TOKEN from GITHUB_TOKEN.
- ci/update-vendored.sh: defaults (`all --version latest --pr --deps=install`), CICD_INPUT_VENDOR / CICD_INPUT_VERSION, `--private` only when CICD_INPUT_PRIVATE=true, GH_TOKEN = VENDOR_PAT else GITHUB_TOKEN; inputs reach `.vendored/install` as arguments and never through a shell (an input like `$(touch pwned); x` arrives verbatim as one argv element and no file is created).
- ci/vendor-check.sh: GITHUB_HEAD_REF set from CICD_SOURCE_BRANCH when unset, kept when set; `--base "$CICD_BASE"` passed to .vendored/check.
- ci/setup.sh: floor read from requires-python; error when unreadable; local fallback to python3 when the floor is missing and CI unset; failure when CI set and no floor (stub PATH so nothing is installed).
- ci/test.sh: uses the venv python when present, python3 with pytest otherwise, error message when pytest missing.
- install.sh: what is written where on a first install and on an upgrade (code under the install dir, config created when missing and preserved on reinstall, schema installed, workflows generated), with fetch_file stubbed to a local mirror as tests/test_install.py `stub_install_sh` does.
Wiring:
- ci/setup.sh installs bats-core (pinned version) into the cache (`${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/git-cicd/`) when `bats` is not on PATH; setup may download, the tests themselves use no network.
- ci/test.sh runs pytest then `bats tests/bats/`; a failing bats test fails the step (replace the final `exec` so both run and either failure fails). When bats is missing locally without setup, print how to install (./git-cicd check --setup) and fail in CI.
- .vendored/configs/git-cicd.json `paths` of the `test` job: already includes `install.sh`, `ci/**`, `tests/**`, so bats files under tests/ need no change; change it only if files land elsewhere, then run `./git-cicd generate` and commit.
- AGENTS.md ("Running the checks", Layout `tests/` line) and README.md "Developing git-cicd" (test row): say the test job runs pytest and the bats tests and setup installs bats.
- Keep the existing pytest tests of these scripts (tests/test_own_jobs.py, tests/test_install.py) — they exercise git-cicd run-job end to end and count toward its coverage.

## Acceptance criteria
- `./git-cicd check --setup` passes in a clean checkout, and its output shows the bats tests running for install.sh and each ci/ script.
- Breaking one case (e.g. editing ci/release.sh to bump on `chore: install`) fails `./git-cicd check --job test`; shown once in the PR description.
- `./git-cicd verify` passes; generated workflows unchanged.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing; no vendor-protected file touched.
- Verdict / git-cicd:verdict passes on the PR.

## Decisions
- bats files live under tests/bats/ so the existing `tests/**` path of the test job covers them and the config/workflows stay unchanged.
- bats-core is installed by ci/setup.sh from a pinned release into the git-cicd cache, mirroring how setup already installs pytest into its venv, so no workflow or Python version changes.
- Existing pytest tests of the shell scripts stay: removing them would lower git-cicd coverage.
